question: What is the meaning of bim object in relation to production data?
description: A BIM object represents a specific instance created from a class, inheriting attributes and methods of that class, and can have its own unique set of attribute values. In relation to production data, a BIM object can store and manage data about the production process, including information about materials, components, and construction activities. This data can be used to track progress, monitor quality, and ensure efficient production processes. BIM objects can also be linked to other objects, such as materials or components, to create a comprehensive digital representation of the production process. This allows for better collaboration, communication, and decision-making among stakeholders involved in the production process. Overall, BIM objects play a crucial role in managing and organizing production data in the context of building information modeling.

BIM models encompass more than just visual representations; they contain critical information that aids stakeholders in accessing, 
evaluating, and utilizing data effectively with proper management [34]. However, due to the fact that there are many software tools 
could lead to significant compatibility challenges. Efficient collaboration and data interchange between the various stakeholders is 
made possible by open standards like Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) and effective data management procedures [1]. BIM models 
constantly change as a result of contributions from the different stakeholders during the course of the project. Version control is 
ensured by effective data management, allowing teams to monitor changes and operate with the most recent data, improving 
transparency and eliminating mistakes [34]. With this variety of contributors to BIM models, data integrity is essential. In order to 
promote the stakeholders’ confidence in decision-making, rigorous data management protocols are required to provide consistent 
information. This is achieved through the building’s lifespan, as efficiency and sustainability are improved, supported by useful in­
sights through the data-rich environment of BIM [1,34].
